verdict.rationale: YYLO's CLI takes a plain-language `--task` description and turns it into a scoped, tracked unit of work (task worktree, ledger record, WORKING state) via `yylo init`/`task start`, which matches the intent-to-spec pattern. However, there's no evidence of NLP/parsing that decomposes a vague feature/bug description into a structured spec with acceptance criteria — the docs assume the developer already writes a 'verifiable outcome' string, and the task creation is closer to task tracking than intent-to-spec transformation. missing for 10: evidence of automatic requirement extraction/clarification, generated acceptance criteria or scoped subtasks from a raw natural-language description, and independent/hands-on validation of this specific flow.
